title: readLock collapses a stat error into absent, so a break file it cannot stat is reported as nonexistent and the lock-removal advice becomes unsafe (QCLI-522 round-2 findings, N2 ranked first)
description:
Findings from the QCLI-522 round-2 FULL review (unit quest-cli-review-657r2, model deepseek-flash, DEC-183 Stage 1), which APPROVED opum-ai/quest-cli#657 at 75506c3a (merged as 38ba9fc5). ITEMS ARE IN RANK ORDER.

N2 (MINOR, first): src/application/tasks/id-allocation.ts:308-309 is `stat(...).catch(() => null)`, which collapses EACCES, EIO and ELOOP into "absent". An unreadable break file then produces a false "No break file exists at ..." -- and since that is the branch that makes removing the lock sound safe, an operator is told the lock can be removed while a live breaker may hold an unreadable break file. Fix: narrow the catch to ENOENT; any other stat error must report the file PRESENT with an unknown age, using the existing "its age could not be read" wording. Correct readLock docblock at :298-300 to match.

N1 (MINOR): the new ENOENT read branch (:314-320) has no test. Add a seam and a case where stat succeeds and readFile throws ENOENT, asserting the hint says no break file exists.

N4 (NIT): breakFileStampedMillisecondsAgo is mtime-derived when the file is zero-byte. Rename it or document that, and pin the semantics in a test.

N5 (NIT): the CHANGELOG says the hint never gives a cause, while the hint itself names a hedged possibility. Reword so the two agree.

N6 (NIT): the dead-pid advice "Remove <break file> first" should add "if it still names pid N", because pid reuse can make that file another process.

N7 (NIT): the path assertions in the hint tests are still toContain, so a path that is a substring of the reported one passes. Assert the exact clause.

N8 (NIT): the unreadable end-to-end fixture cannot tell which of the two unreadable branches ran. Make it distinguish them.

Not to be worked until the day plan names it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The stat catch in readLock is narrowed to ENOENT: any other stat failure reports the break file as PRESENT with an unreadable age using the existing age-could-not-be-read wording, never as absent, and the readLock docblock describes the split
A test drives the seam where stat succeeds and readFile fails with ENOENT, asserting the hint reports that no break file exists
The mtime-derived stamp field is renamed or documented so its meaning is explicit for a zero-byte break file, and a test pins that semantics

The CHANGELOG no longer claims the hint never names a cause, the dead-pid advice is conditional on the file still naming that pid, the path assertions compare the exact clause rather than a substring, and the unreadable end-to-end fixture distinguishes which unreadable branch ran

plan: 1. Narrow the stat catch in readLock to ENOENT: any other stat failure returns a PRESENT holder with an unreadable age (pid null, at null), and rewrite the readLock docblock to describe the split from the readFile ENOENT branch.

2. Make every readLock caller handle an unreadable age safely: breakStaleLock refuses to judge it stale, takeBreakFile never clears it, releaseLock never unlinks on it, and acquireLock carries a null lock/break age into the timeout error.

3. Add an injectable LockReadIo seam (stat + readFile) on IdAllocationRequest and BreakOptions, threaded through acquireLock, breakStaleLock and takeBreakFile, so the stat-then-read window is drivable without racing a real filesystem.

4. Tests in test/qcli522-alloc-lock-break-hint.test.ts, in process with a fake clock: stat throws EACCES for the break path and the hint reports the file PRESENT with its age could not be read; stat succeeds and readFile throws ENOENT and the hint reports no break file exists.

5. Rename the hint input key breakFileStampedMillisecondsAgo to breakFileAgeMilliseconds, document on the error field that a zero-byte file age is mtime-derived, and pin that with utimes in the unreadable end-to-end fixture.

6. Reword the hint dead-pid advice to remove the break file only if it still names that pid, and reword the CHANGELOG claim that the unreadable holder is never given a cause so it agrees with the hedged wording the hint actually prints.

7. Tighten the hint tests: path assertions compare the exact clause rather than a substring, and the unreadable end-to-end fixture asserts branch-specific wording so it distinguishes the write-window branch from the aged branch.
8. Run bun run check with the pinned bun, commit on fix/QCLI-528-lock-read-split, push, open the PR and report its head SHA.
implementationNotes: QCLI-528 (QCLI-522 round-2 findings N2/N1/N4/N5/N6/N7/N8, all addressed). readLock stat catch narrowed to ENOENT: any other stat failure returns a PRESENT holder with pid and age null (an unreadable file is not an absent one), and its docblock states the split from the readFile-ENOENT branch. breakStaleLock refuses an unreadable age so a null cannot fall through a NaN comparison into a break; takeBreakFile never clears on one; acquireLock carries a null lock/break age into the timeout error. New LockReadIo seam (IdAllocationRequest.lockReadIo, BreakOptions.readIo) drives the stat-then-read window in process with a fake clock. input.breakFileStampedMillisecondsAgo renamed to breakFileAgeMilliseconds, and the field doc says a zero-byte break file age comes from its mtime. The dead-pid advice now says remove the break file only if it still names that pid. TESTS: two in-process seam tests (stat EACCES for the break path -> present, age could not be read, hint never says absent; stat succeeds then readFile ENOENT -> hint says no break file exists), one stale-lock test (an unstat-able lock is never broken and the file is untouched), the unreadable end-to-end fixture now sets the zero-byte file mtime 60s back and asserts a 65-120s mtime-derived input age plus the AGED branch wording and the absence of the write-window wording, and every path assertion compares the exact clause. MUTATION EVIDENCE, all three measured and restored, file byte-identical at sha256 3ff9a34a: catch-all stat restored turned the N2 seam test red (1 fail, 1 pass); readFile-ENOENT branch removed turned the N1 test red; holder.at null guard removed turned the stale-lock test red (broke=true, lock removed). bun run check under bun 1.4.3 exit 0 -- typecheck, lint, format, layer, 1304 unit tests and 45 mod tests; the local mod arm reports NOT TYPECHECKED for Claude Code 2.1.308 (no declaration on this machine, pre-existing).
finalSummary: QCLI-528 fixes the QCLI-522 round-2 findings in the allocation-lock timeout hint. readLock stat catch is narrowed to ENOENT, so a break file that exists but cannot be stat d (EACCES, EIO, ELOOP) is reported PRESENT with an unreadable age instead of absent -- the branch that told an operator removing the lock was safe; the docblock states the split from the readFile-ENOENT branch. Every caller handles the unreadable age safely: breakStaleLock refuses to judge it stale, takeBreakFile never clears on it, and the timeout error carries a null age rather than NaN. A new injectable LockReadIo seam drives the stat-then-read window in process with a fake clock. The hint input key breakFileStampedMillisecondsAgo is renamed breakFileAgeMilliseconds and documented as mtime-derived for a zero-byte file; the dead-pid advice now conditions removal on the file still naming that pid; the CHANGELOG no longer claims the hint never names a cause; the hint path assertions compare exact clauses; and the unreadable end-to-end fixture now distinguishes the two unreadable branches and pins the mtime-derived age. Verified: bun run check exit 0 under bun 1.4.3 -- typecheck, lint, format, layer, 1304 unit tests and 45 mod tests (the local mod arm reports NOT TYPECHECKED for Claude Code 2.1.308, pre-existing) -- and three mutation controls each turned their own test red and were restored with the file verified byte-identical.
